subject: Greenshore connectivity chaos — exec escalation & path review
messages:
From: Amit Rao <amit@greenshore.io>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, techops@greenshore.io
Cc: Maya Patel <maya.patel@greenshore.io>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: sudden latency + 502 spike impacting checkout (need exec attention)

Vanessa / Redwood ops,

We started seeing a sharp increase in end-to-end latency and 5xx rates on our checkout path at ~07:45 PT. Error rate jumped from ~0.2% to 4.7% and p99 latency spiked from 180ms to ~1.8s. Customers are reporting failed checkouts.

We believe this may be related to a connectivity change in our VPC peering (we pushed a routing tweak at 07:30) but also observed a cluster of DNS NXDOMAIN timeouts and intermittent 502s from the gateway/proxy layer.

Attached is a short pcap capture taken from our edge collector at 07:48 and a CSV with SLO windows. We need a rapid investigation and executive visibility — looping in Maya. Can Redwood confirm if there were any capacity shifts, routing flips, or active firewall rules that could cause NAT conntrack exhaustion or asymmetric pathing?

We are ready to provide traceroutes and any logs you need. This is causing revenue impact — please escalate.

- Amit Rao
VP Engineering, Greenshore Commerce
[Attachment: network-trace-20270510.pcap (pcap)]
[Attachment: greenshore-slo-spike-summary.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Rao <amit@greenshore.io>
Cc: techops@greenshore.io, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 08:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Urgent: sudden latency + 502 spike impacting checkout (need exec attention)

Amit — thanks for the alert and uploads. I’m escalating internally now. Short plan of attack:

1) Triage: Jonas’ team will look at peering, DNS, and NAT metrics immediately.
2) Mitigation: We can route Greenshore traffic to a warm standby pool (region us-west-2) to reduce NAT pressure — if you want a temporary failover we can flip routing for 10-15 minutes.
3) Exec brief: Vivek and I will prepare a 1-page for Maya summarizing impact & remediation and propose service credit.

Jonas — can you confirm whether any peering reroutes or firewall policy changes were executed from Redwood side between 07:00–08:00 PT? Also please check NAT conntrack and proxy worker backlogs.

Amit — please share a quick traceroute from your edge and any deploy logs around 07:30.

I’ll coordinate an immediate call if needed.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Phone: +1 415-555-0123
[Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RI-8921]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amit Rao <amit@greenshore.io>, techops@greenshore.io
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 08:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Urgent: sudden latency + 502 spike impacting checkout (need exec attention)

Vanessa / Amit — quick preliminary from infra triage:

- No scheduled peering changes on Redwood’s control plane between 06:30–08:00 PT.
- We do see a localized burst of SYN retransmits and increased TCP RTOs on paths to Greenshore’s US-West peering fabric starting 07:32.
- DNS: one of the resolver pools showed elevated query latency (~800ms) and some SERVFAILs correlated with the same time window.
- Proxy layer: worker 12 on the edge cluster experienced queue growth and 502s; evidence points to upstream connection resets likely from transient NAT exhaustion on a border firewall appliance.

Immediate asks for Greenshore:
- Can you confirm whether the 07:30 routing tweak changed source IP ranges or introduced a new NATing hop?
- Please provide traceroute and public resolver IPs used.

Mitigation steps we can take now (low-risk):
1) Warm failover to us-west-2 pool to spread connections (temporary).
2) Increase proxy worker concurrency and temporarily relax connection timeout to reduce resets.
3) Spin up an extra NAT appliance in the peering zone (if you approve temporary capacity).

I’m attaching a short text dump of the TCP trace headers we captured.

— Jonas
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: tcp-header-dump.txt (text)]

From: Amit Rao <amit@greenshore.io>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: techops@greenshore.io, Maya Patel <maya.patel@greenshore.io>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Urgent: sudden latency + 502 spike impacting checkout (need exec attention)

Jonas — thanks, that aligns with what we see. We did a route tweak at 07:30 that consolidated flows behind a new NAT gateway (to simplify our egress audit). That likely reduced source IP variety and increased per-NAT connection density. We didn’t expect to hit conntrack limits.

Traceroute from an affected host attached. We also rolled a minor deploy at 07:20 (small change to checkout path cache TTLs) — not sure if that’s related but calls it out.

We would like Redwood to:
- Execute warm failover to us-west-2 immediately.
- Temporarily increase proxy worker concurrency and apply the relaxed timeout.

We’re on standby to flip routing if Redwood needs us to.

- Amit

[Attachment: traceroute-greenshore-07-48.txt (text)]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@greenshore.io>, Amit Rao <amit@greenshore.io>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Greenshore incident — exec summary and proposed customer remedy

Maya / Amit — following our triage and the temporary mitigations last night, here’s a concise summary for execs: 

Incident summary:
- Impact window: 07:30–08:15 PT on 2027-05-10.
- Symptoms: p99 latency increased to ~1.8s; 5xx rate up to 4.7%; checkout failures reported.
- Root cause (prelim): Increased NAT connection density from Greenshore routing change + transient resolver timeouts; resulted in upstream connection resets and proxy worker queue growth.

What we did:
- Warm failover to us-west-2 pool at 08:00 (reduced NAT density).
- Increased proxy concurrency and extended timeouts; spun an additional NAT appliance in peering zone.
- Monitored for 2 hours; SLOs returned to baseline by ~09:50 PT.

Customer remedy proposal:
1) One-time service credit equivalent to 10% of April 2027 hosted inference bill (pending accounting).
2) Joint postmortem with Greenshore and Redwood infra (next 48 hours).
3) Run a joint load-and-failure test to validate peering/NAT sizing.

Next steps — owners:
- Jonas (Redwood infra): deliver postmortem draft to Amit by EOD 2027-05-11.
- Marissa (CS): finalize credit with finance; present terms.
- Vanessa / Vivek: coordinate exec brief and sign-off.

We take this seriously and will produce the postmortem and remediation plan.

— Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Product & Operations, Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
[Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RI-8921]

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Rao <amit@greenshore.io>, Maya Patel <maya.patel@greenshore.io>

Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 16:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Greenshore incident — exec summary and proposed customer remedy

Amit / Maya — thank you for your partnership here and for the quick traceroutes/traces. Attached is the exec brief we shared internally and the proposed credit terms. Jonas’ postmortem draft is linked in the Jira and we’ll run the joint load test next week (dates TBD).

Key decisions confirmed:
- Temporary mitigations completed and validated.
- Service credit: ten percent of April invoice; Marissa will confirm final amount with finance.
- Postmortem due to Amit and Maya by EOD 2027-05-11 (Jonas owner).
- Joint remediation: schedule runbook review and peering sizing test (Jonas + Greenshore techops).

If you’d like me to escalate further to Redwood’s CEO, tell me now — otherwise Vivek and I will handle the exec sync.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
